description: Implement the per-finding workflow spec described in docs/per-finding-workflow.md, following the two-phase plan in docs/per-finding-workflow-plan.md.

userStories.title: Phase 1 — Delete virtual entries and expanders
userStories.description:
As a maintainer, I need to remove the entries/expanders abstraction from the linter so subsequent per-finding runtime work lands on a smaller surface.
This is a standalone commit with no new features. Every existing integration test must pass unchanged; this isolates a large deletion diff from the per-finding runtime that follows.

Scope:
- Delete entries/base-entry.ts, entries/file-entry.ts, entries/json-array-entry.ts.
- Delete expanders/base-expander.ts, expanders/file-expander.ts, expanders/json-array-expander.ts.
- checks/base-check.ts: remove the expander field, remove expand() and setExpander(), remove supportsInMemory / lintInMemory / fixInMemory / lintAndFixInMemory.
- registry.ts: remove builtinExpanders export and the expander section from --help.
- linter.ts: replace runEntryLint / runEntryFix helpers with direct check.lint(file, ...) / check.fix(file, ...) calls; remove entry expansion loops so every check receives whole file paths.
- Config loader: reject any 'expander' block in linter-config.json at load with message '<check>: \'expander\' is no longer supported. See docs/per-finding-workflow.md.' and exit 2.
acceptanceCriteria: yarn test — all existing integration tests pass unchanged (no snapshot updates).
grep -rn 'expander\|Entry\|Expander' --include='*.ts' returns only test-fixture matches and the config-load error string.
yarn build succeeds and dist/linter.mjs is committed alongside the source change.
No files remain under entries/ or expanders/.
checks/base-check.ts no longer references expander, expand, setExpander, supportsInMemory, lintInMemory, fixInMemory, or lintAndFixInMemory.
registry.ts no longer exports builtinExpanders and --help output no longer mentions expanders.
linter.ts no longer references runEntryLint or runEntryFix; checks are invoked directly with whole file paths.
Loading a linter-config.json that declares an 'expander' block exits 2 with the spec's error message on stderr.
Commit is standalone: no per-finding runtime, no new CLI flags, no new config keys, no new fixtures.
userStories.notes: Companion spec: docs/per-finding-workflow.md. Detailed checklist: docs/per-finding-workflow-plan.md#phase-1--delete-virtual-entries--expanders. If any behaviour disagrees with the spec, the spec wins — update the plan md, not the spec.

userStories.title: Phase 2 — Per-finding runtime (types, runner, CLI, config, PRD gen, RegexCheck, tests)
userStories.description:
As a maintainer, I need to implement the per-finding runtime end-to-end in one cohesive commit: findings type, runner invariant, --expect-max and --show CLI modes, config keys, PRD generation for per-finding mode, RegexCheck migration, and every integration test the spec's Test Coverage section names.

Scope (see docs/per-finding-workflow-plan.md#phase-2--per-finding-runtime for the full checklist):
- Types: declare interface CheckFinding { message: string; snippet: string; startLine?: number; endLine?: number; } in checks/base-check.ts; extend CheckResult with optional findings?: CheckFinding[].
- Runner: preflight-grep for existing checks that return pass with an output shape; enforce universal invariant (status pass ⇔ findings.length == 0); synthesize a single finding on fail/error when the check omits one; populate empty snippet from startLine/endLine (display only); widen failedPairs to Array<{ file, checkName, finding }>.
- CLI --expect-max <N>: --lint only; exactly one --checks and one --files; reject combos with --fix, --output-prd, --show; reject negative or non-integer N; exit 0 when findings ≤ N, exit 1 when >, exit 2 for unknown check / check-not-in-mode / missing file; exit-1 output lists remaining findings (message + line range + snippet).
- CLI --show <mode>: --lint only; only accepted mode is 'first' (others exit 2, reserved); exactly one --checks and one --files; reject combos with --fix, --expect-max, --output-prd; output one line of JSON { startLine, endLine, snippet, message } or the literal null when zero findings, exit 0 in both cases; deterministic ordering (ascending startLine, then check's original emit order); implement the snippet widening algorithm exactly (2+2 baseline, extend by 1+1 until unique, cap at 20+20, include "unique": false at cap); widening is scoped to --show output only and never affects count or --expect-max.
- Config loader: add prd.storySplitMode ('per-file' | 'per-finding', default 'per-file') and prd.findingsPerStory (positive integer, default 1); hard errors (exit 2) for unknown storySplitMode value, per-finding + prd.group, per-finding + filesPerStory != 1, per-finding + findingsPerStory <= 0 or non-integer; load-time warning (stderr, exit 0) when findingsPerStory is set with storySplitMode absent or per-file.
- PRD generation: per-file mode dedupes multiple findings per (file, check) back to one story before applying filesPerStory (byte-identical output to today for every current fixture); per-finding mode groups findings by (check, file), for each group with M findings emits S = ceil(M/N) ordered stories K = 1..S with budget Nₖ = min(N, M - (K-1)*N) and acceptance criterion <baseCommand> --lint --checks <check> --files <file> --expect-max <max(0, M - K*N)>; PRD ordering: files alphabetical, checks in config order, stories in K order.
- Title generator: M == 1 → 'Fix <check> in <file>:<startLine>' (fall back to 'Fix <check> in <file>' if no line info); S == 1 && M > 1 → 'Fix <check> in <file> (M findings)'; S > 1 → 'Fix <check> in <file> (story K of S; Nₖ findings)'.
- Description generator: emit the spec's default workflow body verbatim with substituted <file>, <check>, M, K, N, Nₖ, and <max(0, M - K*N)>.
- Template placeholders: keep {file}, {files}, {fileCount}, {check}; add {findingCount}, {storyCount}, {storyIndex}, {storyBudget}, {expectMax}, {startLine}, {endLine}, {message}, {snippet}, {findings}, {workflow}.
- RegexCheck migration: emit one CheckFinding per regex hit (message = configured message, snippet = matched line, startLine = endLine = hit's line number); keep the existing output string ('N hit(s):\n  line 1: ...') byte-identical; run a byte-identity gate (yarn test --grep regex-process-env-ban with zero diff) immediately after the change.
acceptanceCriteria: node .linter/linter.mjs --lint --checks no-ts-as-operator,no-ts-any-type,tsc --files checks/base-check.ts,checks/regex-check.ts,linter.ts
checks/base-check.ts declares interface CheckFinding { message: string; snippet: string; startLine?: number; endLine?: number; } and CheckResult has an optional findings?: CheckFinding[] field.

Runner enforces the universal invariant: any check that returns status pass with a non-empty findings array is treated as a runner error; any fail/error without findings gets a synthesized [{ message: res.output ?? 'check failed', snippet: '' }].
Runner populates empty snippet from startLine/endLine by reading the file range for display; count semantics never depend on the snippet.
failedPairs is Array<{ file, checkName, finding }> with finding always populated.

--expect-max <N> is accepted only with --lint, requires exactly one --checks and exactly one --files, rejects negative or non-integer N, and rejects combinations with --fix, --output-prd, and --show (each misuse → exit 2).
--expect-max <N> exits 0 when findings.length ≤ N, exit 1 when >, exit 2 for unknown check / check-not-in-mode / missing file. Exit-1 output lists remaining findings (message + line range + snippet).

--show <mode> is accepted only with --lint, requires exactly one --checks and one --files, and rejects combinations with --fix, --expect-max, and --output-prd (each misuse → exit 2). Only accepted value is 'first'; any other value → exit 2.

--show first prints one line of JSON { startLine, endLine, snippet, message } for the earliest finding, or the literal null when zero findings; exit 0 in both cases. Findings are ordered by ascending startLine with ties broken by the check's original emit order; two runs of the same input produce byte-identical output.

Snippet widening: starts at 2 lines above and 2 below clipped at file boundaries; extends by 1+1 until unique with cap at 20+20; when uniqueness is not reached at the cap the JSON includes "unique": false and the snippet is the maximally widened window. Widening never affects on-disk snippet, count, or --expect-max.
Config loader accepts prd.storySplitMode ('per-file' | 'per-finding', default 'per-file') and prd.findingsPerStory (positive integer, default 1).
Config loader exits 2 for: unknown storySplitMode value (stderr lists valid values); per-finding + prd.group; per-finding + filesPerStory != 1; per-finding + findingsPerStory <= 0 or non-integer.
Config loader emits stderr warning (exit 0) 'findingsPerStory is ignored when storySplitMode is not per-finding' when findingsPerStory is set with storySplitMode absent or 'per-file'.

PRD per-file mode dedupes multiple findings per (file, check) back to one story before applying filesPerStory; all existing PRD fixture snapshots (prd-single-file-multi-hit, prd-two-files-two-stories, prd-no-failures, …) remain byte-identical.

PRD per-finding mode groups findings by (check, file) and, for M findings with N = findingsPerStory, emits S = ceil(M/N) ordered stories K = 1..S with budget Nₖ = min(N, M - (K-1)*N) and acceptance criterion '<baseCommand> --lint --checks <check> --files <file> --expect-max <max(0, M - K*N)>'.
PRD ordering: files alphabetical; within a file, checks in config order; within (check, file), stories in K order.

Title generator: M == 1 → 'Fix <check> in <file>:<startLine>' (fallback 'Fix <check> in <file>' without line info); S == 1 && M > 1 → 'Fix <check> in <file> (M findings)'; S > 1 → 'Fix <check> in <file> (story K of S; Nₖ findings)'.
Description generator emits the spec's default workflow body verbatim with substituted <file>, <check>, M, K, N, Nₖ, and <max(0, M - K*N)>.

Template placeholders {findingCount}, {storyCount}, {storyIndex}, {storyBudget}, {expectMax}, {startLine}, {endLine}, {message}, {snippet}, {findings}, {workflow} are supported alongside the existing {file}, {files}, {fileCount}, {check}.

RegexCheck emits one CheckFinding per regex hit with message = configured message, snippet = matched line, startLine = endLine = hit's line number; the existing 'N hit(s):\n  line 1: ...' output string is byte-identical.
Byte-identity gate: yarn test --grep regex-process-env-ban passes with zero snapshot diff immediately after the RegexCheck change.
New integration fixtures exist and pass: per-finding-single, per-finding-multi-n1, per-finding-multi-nk-remainder, per-finding-multi-nk-divisible, per-finding-fallback, per-finding-sequential-drift.

New config-validation fixtures exist and pass: config-storysplit-unknown, config-per-finding-with-group, config-per-finding-with-files-per-story, config-findings-per-story-invalid, config-findings-per-story-warning.

New --expect-max fixtures exist and pass: lint-expect-max-pass, lint-expect-max-fail, lint-expect-max-misuse (one fixture per: --fix combo, 0 or 2 --checks, 0 or 2 --files, negative N, non-integer N, combo with --output-prd, combo with --show, unknown check, check-not-in-mode, missing file).

New --show first fixtures exist and pass: lint-show-first-json, lint-show-first-null, lint-show-first-widening-initial, lint-show-first-widening-extended, lint-show-first-widening-capped, lint-show-first-determinism, lint-show-first-misuse (one fixture per: --fix combo, --expect-max combo, --output-prd combo, 0 or 2 --checks, 0 or 2 --files, --show bogus, unknown check, check-not-in-mode, missing file).
New RegexCheck fixture exists and passes: regex-emits-findings (asserts CheckFinding[] is populated on a failing file).

yarn test — every existing integration test still passes without snapshot updates. Every existing check (tsc, encoding, always-fail, ai-prompt, firecrawl, composite, custom, crlf) runs unchanged; only RegexCheck source is touched among the checks.
yarn build succeeds and dist/linter.mjs is committed alongside the source change.
The TypeScript 'as' operator remains banned; use proper typing or type guards, and use @ts-expect-error only where idiomatic typing is infeasible.
The TypeScript 'any' type remains banned; prefer 'unknown' plus type guards when the type is genuinely open.
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 (virtual entries/expanders removal). Companion spec: docs/per-finding-workflow.md. Detailed checklist: docs/per-finding-workflow-plan.md#phase-2--per-finding-runtime. If any behaviour disagrees with the spec, the spec wins — update the plan md, not the spec. Phase 3 items (tsc/encoding/crlf migrations, ralph runner integration, --show all, --json) are explicitly out of scope here.
